title.narrative: Education for Employment Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The proposed Education for Employment Sector Development Program (EESDP) will strengthen human capital in the Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) and support inclusive growth and economic diversification. The policy-based loan will support reforms to align secondary education, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and higher education with the country's workforce needs. This includes enhancing the role of secondary education in preparing youth for employment. The investment project will build capacity in the Ministry of Education and Sport (MOES) to align secondary education, TVET, and higher education with skill demand. It will also enhance the quality and relevance of secondary education and increase completion rates. EESDP builds on the Asian Development Bank (ADB) Secondary Education Sector Development Program (SESDP) and related support for TVET and higher education.

c. By mid-2025, shares of female and male (i) lower secondary graduates and (ii) upper secondary graduates in education, training and/or nonagricultural wage employment increased by at least 5 percentage points to X% and Y%, respectively (Baseline for graduates in 2019 to be determined through surveys in 2020 and 2021) Progress/Status: Not yet due. Continuous monitoring. Assessment in 2025. ================== The project conducted a youth NEET survey in 2021; the results showed that 27.6% of boys and 29.7% of girls are NEET. Another secondary tracer study will be conducted in November 2025. the results will use to compare with the results conducted in 2021. The baseline data for LSE graduates in 2019 and USE graduates in 2020 were determined through sample surveys in 2020 and 2021. For LSE, the baseline is 79.66% (81.23% for boys; 78.14% for girls). Among the LSE graduates in SY 2019 and 2020, 17% were employed, 7% were unemployed and 76% were out of the labor force. Among the employed LSE graduates, 31% were in Non-Agricultural Wage Employment. For USE, the baseline is 45.25% (40.95% for boys; 49.33% for girls). Among the USE graduates, 17% were employed, 8% were unemployed and 75% were out of the labor force. Among the employed USE graduates, 58% were in Non-Agricultural Wage Employment.
Enrollment in secondary education has gradually declined and the dropout rate has increased since 2019 due to myriad reasons. The most prevalent ones exacerbated and/or brought about by the school disruptions and economic impacts of COVID-19, include: (i) a lower pipeline of students graduating from primary levels; (ii) difficult financial situations for families unable to pay associated school costs; (iii) the opportunity costs for young people to support their family income; and (iv) lack of motivation due to not seeing a brighter future after graduation. Many youth in USE opt for low-skilled jobs in neighboring countries where the jobs are more available. These factors for dropout stem from the root causes of the nationwide economic shock. ===================== The project together with HRDO undertook the NEET in 2021 and the results showed 27% of boys and 29.7 girls. This was quoted as the baseline for the outcome indicator c.
The project provides stipend and short-term skills training programs to both LSE and USE students to equip them with marketable skills to keep the students continuing until graduation and reduce the NEET rate.
The project will conduct another endline tracer study in November 2025 to assess the graduate's trajectories and reduce drop-out rate. The results will cover the LSE and USE graduates in SY 2025/26. The results will be used to assess the achievement of this outcome at the project completion. Data Source: MOES tracer studies for lower secondary and upper secondary graduates in 2024 Baseline value: TBD 2020/21 survey

Output: Equitable secondary education access and completion increased Indicator: Project by 2024 - 60 schools provided with new classroom blocks (including science laboratories and libraries), sex-segregated dormitories, and sanitation facilities (2018 baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: On track to meet target
• 45 school blocks were completed, 12 are ongoing, and 3 are new • 25 dormitories were completed, and 9 are ongoing, and 2 are new
================== Twelve civil works contracts have been awarded, comprising 57 schools. Procurement of works for 3 additional schools is ongoing. ================== Eight, out of 12 civil works packages for the 60 schools to be provided with new classroom blocks (including science laboratories and libraries), sex-segregated dormitories, and sanitation facilities have been completed. The remaining packages are expected to be awarded by Q1 2024.
================= Construction of 12 schools and dormitories have been delayed due to poor performance of contractors and raining season.
(i) Kouan District: the construction has been delayed for almost 2 years due to (i) the contractor encountering cash flow issues, (ii) shortage of workers and (iii) unavailability of site engineers. (ii) Nambak District: The contractor in Nambak district submitted the 4th request for an extension of the completion date. The project agreed and endorsed the request. The contractor could not provide an extension of the bank guarantee for 10% of the total contract because it did not have the sufficient deposit amount required by the bank. =================
There are a remaining 15 schools under progress: Civil works with significant delays • Ta Oi (three secondary schools)-CW02: The status is 69% versus 60% as per the revised work plan, the expected completion date is 30 April 2025, three months earlier than the contract completion date. • Nambak (three secondary schools)-CW8: The status is 89% versus 91% as per the revised work plan (two schools are 100% completed and two schools are ongoing), the expected completion date is 31 December 2024, as per the contract. • Kuan (five secondary schools)-CW12: Civil works for this contract are significantly delayed, and three requests for extension have been approved. ADB recently endorsed the third request for an extension until April 2025. Monitoring records show that the current progress is 71% against the schedule of 74%. This means an average progress of only 1.3% per month against the target of 7%. If this progress continues, the contractor will complete the construction in 24 months, which is beyond the project closing date. The mission suggested that the DGE seek guidance from the ministry on how to solve the problem. The options discussed are: (i) inform the contractor that no more extensions will be allowed and run the risk of further delays and non-completion, and/or (ii) terminate the contract and proceed with a request for quotations. If the latter, the architect consultant can assess the remaining works and prepare the BOQ for each school. The request for quotations can be divided into five packages. The mission will seek advice from ADB's procurement specialist on option 2.
Civil works progress under packages 13, 14 and 15 • Singpatthana Secondary School-CW13 (new): The status is 3.40% versus 9.17% as per the work plan, the expected completion date is 31 August 2025. • Nakhone Secondary School-CW14 (new): The status is 9.58% versus 5.72% as per the work plan, the expected completion date is 31 August 2025. • Darkdeun Secondary School-CW15 (new): The status is 89.80% versus 87.96% as per the revised work plan, the expected completion date is 31 January 2025.
Ten out of twenty-five dormitory blocks were completed, the remaining 15 blocks are under construction.
Data Source: MOES M&E reports Actual value:

Output: Equitable secondary education access and completion increased Indicator: Project by 2024 - Stipends provided to at least 2,400 disadvantaged students in 12 districts (2019 baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Completed
2,400 students from poor and vulnerable were provided stipend, as of July 2024, 2,376 remained in stipend program. 20 recipients drop out (9 females /11males) and 4 recipients (3 females/1 male) transferred to other schools, which are not in the list of EESDP beneficiaries. ================== The project has provided a stipend of LAK 150,000 (currently $7 due to depreciation of the Lao Kip) per month to 2,221 disadvantaged and ethnic minority students. Originally, 2,400 recipients were selected according to agreed criteria, however 179 students (95 girls) either relocated to non-project schools or dropped out.
The Mission notes areas for improvement of efficiency and effectiveness in the stipend program. For the disbursement to students, there are delays in the release to school accounts, school principals then require funds for gas to travel to the closest bank to withdraw cash, which is a challenge in remote areas and where the stipend provided to small number of students. In addition to the delayed payments, the amount is also not sufficient for many students to be a strong enough factor to prevent dropout. Despite the constraints, the dropout rate for stipend recipients is lower than those of other students in the EESDP schools and the national average. In Q3 2023, ADB approved additional 922 beneficiaries for the stipends program.
===========================
The project team submitted a proposal to the minister for approval to increase the stipend amount from Kip 200,000 to Kip 300,000 to allow the students have sufficient money to buy education materials and lunch.
Administration fees are now provided to school management to better facilitate disbursement of the stipends with more timely disbursement to the students. ============================== In Dec 2024: The increase of stipend amount from LAK 150,000 to LAK 300,000 was approved. The approved amount will be applied in January 2025. The project identified the highest dropout rates for stipends in Grades 8, 9 and 11 (M3, M2, and M6), with a notable gender disparity in dropout rates.
Data Source: MOES M&E reports Actual value:

Output: Quality and relevance of secondary education to emerging skills demands strengthened Indicator: Project: At least 12,000 teachers of priority subjects received INSET training to deliver the improved curriculum (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Achieved.
By September 2024, 17,535 (person times) teachers were trained to deliver the improved curriculum using new pedagogies to improve teaching and learning.
=========================
In Q1 2022, certification program for the learner-centered approach was developed; and coaching and mentoring in 6 TTCs and 2 FOEs were conducted. ========================= The project has provided in-service training to 6,827 teachers (3,539 women) against a target of 12,000 on learner-centred pedagogy and using the new teacher guides. Webinars during COVID were also provided on this training for 7,359 teachers (3,442 female). Master trainers are being trained and certified to cascade the training. The training for teachers in the remaining schools is expected to be completed by Q4 2025. ========================== In-service training has been delivered to 8,228 teachers (4,206 women), and the remaining of 3,772 teachers will be training in December 2024. They are trained how to use more effective school-based training methodology with follow up coaching and mentoring to ensure learner-centred pedagogy is implemented. Class observations to assess the trained teachers will be conducted to assess if new teaching methods will be applied and the update teacher guide are useful and easily to follow. ==========================
Dec 2024: class observations and follow-up activities were conducted to determine if the trainees fully understand the content of the revised teacher guides and can apply the new teaching approaches. In a field visit during the loan review mission, it was learned that some teachers still use traditional teaching methods instead of the student-centered approach because they have not fully understood the content of the teacher guides. Consequently, they lack confidence in conducting and managing classes as indicated in the teacher guides. The mission recommended that the PMU and DTT should immediately form a team to assess the impact of using the revised teacher guides, with recommendations by December 2025. The report will guide the DTT on how to improve the implementation of INSET, as it is a core activity to enhance the quality of secondary education, alongside the provision of textbooks and learning materials.
The project also conducted training for a total of 1,554 school principals, including 233 (15%) female and 211 (14%) ethnic teachers. However, the mission also learned that school principals have not yet initiated mechanisms for coaching, peer-peer leaning, or follow-up on the application of the new teaching approach. To address this, the PMU, in collaboration with concerned departments, has initiated the appointment of district pedagogy advisers to follow up through class observations and support the trainee teachers. This approach is being implemented instead of enforcing the follow-up mechanism under the training program for school principals. The PMU ensures that the follow-up mechanism will be implemented and evaluated to determine if refresher training is needed. The findings will be shared with Post-Basic Education Focal Groups for comments and validation in January 2026. The draft report will be finalized in February 2026. Data Source: MOES monitoring reports Actual value:

The indicators will be revisited during midterm review.
This data will be tracked in 2024 through EMIS. Current data will be reported after school construction completed. ======================== The project's largest challenge at mid-term review pertains to enrollment and completion nationwide, as well as to enrollment in 60 secondary schools that should increase to at least 42,000 (at least 45% females) (output 3b). Enrolment in SY 2022/23 for the project schools is 25,473 students (12,185 or 47.8% female), below the 2018 baseline of 33,700 students (15,000 female). To address this issue, the project will launch an inclusively designed multimedia information campaign informed by gender- and IP-disaggregated data directed to communities on the importance and relevance of completing secondary education. The project will support the development of a remedial support program that will enable students with a short-term absence to return to school. Data Source: MOES M&E reports Actual value:

Output: Alignment of post-primary education with labor market demand strengthened Indicator: Project: By 2024, partnerships linking secondary schools, TVET, nonformal education centers, and local industries piloted in the secondary school clusters (2019 baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: On track to meet target.
Partnering model arrangements has been implemented. Two models: summer school vacation program and parallel general education + skills training are being implemented. More than 1,200 high school student participate these training programs. Tracking of these trainees will be developed and the findings will be included in the project quarterly reports.
===================== Two models of partnerships linking secondary schools, TVET, nonformal education centers and local industries are being piloted (output 1d). One model takes place in parallel with the school year; and the other is offered during the school vacation break. This activity, by providing students with a base of skills for gainful employment, was identified as a priority to increase the relevance and attractiveness of secondary education. ====================== As of July 2024, a total of 2,476 students have enrolled in partnering program between secondary schools and vocational centers and non-formal centers, of which 1,392 (56%) are girls. The Mission visited TVCVP (Vang Vieng campus) and Vientiane Province TVET College (main campus) in Viengkham Village. The mission through conversations with the school management teams, teachers and students found that the TVET colleges are conducting the programs well and eager to partners with the project. With the basic skills training, students can help with family businesses or obtain part-time jobs, which many report they use to support travel cost and lunch. The mission observed that implementation costs are high and may not be sustainable beyond the project, especially for the monthly stipends, which are significantly higher than the current stipend amount provided by the government. The mission strongly recommended the project to develop a tracking system for the trainees of each batch, monitoring students' returning to school, graduation, and entering the workforce. The findings should be reflected in the following project progress reports, and will be used to evaluate if the partnership programs are viable for investment and to be further supported by ADB, other development partners and/or private sector.
===================== As of December 2024, a total of 2,492 students have enrolled in a partnering program. This includes 580 USE students (326 female) who joined the parallel program and 1,912 LSE students (290 female) who joined the summer program. The selected TVET colleges established a WhatsApp group to monitor their students and found that all students returned to their schools after completing their training. The mission discussed with the PMU the need to establish a tracking system of those trainees and analyze the data compared to the budget invested in this program by October 2025. The analysis will show MOES whether it is justified to scale up this program. The results will also be used for preparing the project completion report in June 2026. Data Source: Monitoring reports of Education for Employment Sector Development Program Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

97,344 copies of teacher's guides (36,380 copies for M1; 36,380 copies for M2; and 24,584 copies for M5) were printed and delivered to all secondary schools. A transport services company was engaged to deliver the books directly to schools in May 2023.
29,104 copies of M3 and 21,072 copies of M6 TGs were delivered to schools in March 2024; bringing the books distributed total = 147,520 copies.
M4 and M7 TGs are currently being finalized by RIES for printing. Printing advertisement was submitted by PMU to MOES for approval and will be submitted to ADB for approval targeting printing in September 2024.
=================================== New SE curricula were developed for 57 schools including TGs for M1, M2 and M5 in Q3 2021. Final TGs for M1, M2 and M5 and drafts of M3, M4, M6 and M7 TGs have been introduced to schools in Q3 2022. Final M3, M4, M6 and M7 TGs will be introduced by Q3 2023.
Use of loan savings is being explored to develop textbooks and/or update the curricula to reflect the learner-centered approach, soft skills, and updated content from the current versions in use from 2009 (LSE) and 2011(USE). ======================== The curriculum for four lower secondary and six upper secondary priority subjects has been revised and introduced to schools through new teachers guides. To date, 97,344 copies of teacher's guides were printed and delivered. The new curriculum is still pending official MOES approval although the teachers guides follow the revised version. ========================= The Project supported the revision of six core subjects. However, the Research Institute for Educational Sciences (RIES) cannot approve the curriculum in its entirety without revising the remaining subjects. In late November 2024, the DGE conducted a workshop to discuss the curriculum revision for other subjects. Approval from the Committee for the Approval of Curriculum and Instructional Materials (CACIM) is expected by December 2024.
Teacher guides for the six priority subjects for Grades 6, 7, 8,10 and 11 were distributed to schools in 2022 and 2023. The teacher guides for Grades 9 and 12 are currently being printed and will be distributed in early 2025.
RIES has committed to completing Grade 6 through Grade 12 textbooks at a rate of 2 months per textbook, with a target completion date of October 2025. Draft manuscripts of textbooks for all grades except for Grades 8, 9 and 12 have been completed for review and finalization by RIES. The mission during the loan review in Dec 2024 discussed with RIES and confirmed that the finalization of textbooks for Grades 6, 7 and 10 will be completed by June 2025, while those for the remaining grades will be completed in October 2025. This timeline will allow sufficient time for procurement and delivery of the textbooks by March 2026. PMU completed 9 out of 12 civil works packages and will proceed with the procurement of new science equipment and library materials to 60 secondary schools and to at least 50 secondary school clusters.
================== Procurement of equipment will commenced soon after completion of the civil works. ================== List of science and library materials were finalized and ready to procure. 120 schools (60 project schools and 50 cluster schools) will receive computer to be used for teaching ITC subject, teachers will used to prepare lesson-plans. Procurement plan is being finalized.
==================
The list of laboratory equipment has been finalized, and procurement of this package is complete. The equipment is expected to be delivered to 101 project schools and cluster schools on 7 January 2025. Training on the use of this equipment will be organized in April 2025. Procurement for an additional 21 schools will be arranged in February 2025, with delivery expected in April 2025. During a field visit in December 2024, the mission found that the equipment was not used because teachers had not received adequate training. Some teachers received only demonstrations instead of hands-on practice, leading to a lack of confidence in conducting experiments or demonstrations for their students. As a result, the chemistry supplies remained unpacked. The mission suggested that the PMU discuss with the supplier the possibility of increasing the number training sessions in smaller groups to ensure each teacher can conduct experiments and understand how to use the equipment properly. Additional training expenses can be arranged through contract variations. The request for contract variation should be submitted to ADB for endorsement in mid -January 2025. Procurement of lab equipment for the additional 21 schools will be arranged in February 2025. MOES Decree No. 3805 on classroom-based assessment (CBA) was approved by MOES in August 8, 2023. The CBA manual was developed by the DGE in close collaboration with the RIES and the DTE with assistance for PIC, improving the student assessment system in secondary school from 90% test-based to now, 70% test-based; adding participation/task performance and projects as basis for assessment. Such 20% difference in the way student learning is assessed is expected to improve as the country gradually shifts to more modern teaching, using the learner-centered approach as the key philosophy.
================================== Classroom-based assessment for INSET has been completed in 2021. A workshop on CBA was conducted in Q4 2022.
================================== In 2023, the Ministry of Education and Sports (MOES) approved the CBA manual developed by the Department of General Education (DGE), which then began training master trainers.
By 2025, DGE had conducted training sessions for secondary school teachers from 60 schools across eight provinces, totaling 491 participants. However, the effectiveness of CBA training needs improvement. To address this, CBA will be integrated with teaching and learning activities to ensure they are implemented effectively in classrooms, emphasizing a learner-centered approach. The DGE, alongside pedagogical advisors, will provide cluster-based training, incorporating CBA through coaching and mentoring to enhance the skills of teachers.
